prompt:
Paint ONE finished frame of a film-like cutscene of our hand-painted point-and-click adventure game 'Posledny zvonec' (Slovakia; eras 1960, 1982, 1995, 2020, 2035). The reference images are numbered in the order they are given: Image 1: place reference: a village culture hall stage with a curtain (repaint in colour, no people) Image 2: place reference: a small wooden stage (no people) Image 3: character reference: Rudo, 34, the amateur actor in his oversized stage costume Image 4: character reference: Lida, 43, the costume maker Image 5: a finished interior painting from our game; use it only for the painting technique, brushwork, palette and line quality, not for its content

Shot: Rehearsal in an empty village culture hall in 1960: on the small wooden stage in front of a painted cloth forest backdrop, Rudo in his far too big checked jacket and low bowler hat stands with one arm flung out and chest forward, delivering his first line grandly and completely for the first time. In the front row below the stage Lida sits on a wooden chair, a hand pressed over her mouth, eyes squeezed, shoulders shaking as she holds back her laughter. Rows of empty chairs.

Characters in this frame (briefs of the approved designs): Rudolf Pavlík, a 34-year-old Slovak amateur actor at a village rehearsal in 1960: grand stage diction, shy off stage. A thin, friendly, slightly anxious clean-shaven face, short dark hair, lanky build. He wears his stage costume: a far too big brown-and-beige checked jacket whose wide shoulders hang over his own and whose sleeves cover half of his hands, a too-big black bowler hat that sits low on his head, a white shirt with a small dark bow tie, baggy brown trousers and worn brown shoes. His arms hang at his sides, the too-long sleeves covering his hands down to the fingertips. No text or logo anywhere. Lída Fialová, a 43-year-old Slovak costume maker of the village amateur theatre in 1960: organised, lively and quick. A warm, lively face with bright attentive eyes and a quick smile, dark brown hair set in a short wavy early-1960s perm. She wears a hand-knitted rust-red (terracotta) wool pullover with three-quarter sleeves over a white blouse collar, a fitted dark navy wool skirt to just below the knee, light stockings and low black shoes. A small silver sewing thimble hangs on a thin black cord around her neck and rests on the front of the pullover. Her hands are loosely clasped at her waist. No text or logo anywhere.

Light and time: Warm stage lights on Rudo, the hall in soft afternoon shade.

Character references show approved characters of the game on a plain grey card: copy each person's face, age, hair, body proportions, clothes and colours exactly, but pose and light them for this scene; never copy the grey card, the sheet layout or a duplicate of the same person. Place references show the real location and its painted version in our game: keep its architecture, materials and era. Photos are only references: repaint everything in our style, paint any real people in them out, and do not copy brand logos or shop names. Composition: a calm 16:9 picture like a still from the last minutes of a film, with a clear focal point and depth; it is shown whole with a caption below it, so keep the subject well inside the frame. One single image: no panels, no split screen, no border, no frame, no captions, no subtitles, no speech bubbles, no watermark, no UI, unless the shot asks for it. No text or lettering anywhere unless the shot quotes it exactly.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
